principle: Examples illustrate transferable creative decisions, not mandatory templates.

examples.clue: Lush large visor, as it were (2,2,5)
examples.surface: An apparently descriptive phrase about an oversized visor
examples.lesson: A seamless surface can disguise a multi-part charade.
A short natural instruction can hide containment.

examples.clue: H I J K L M N O (5)
examples.definition: Entire clue operates as lateral definition
examples.lesson: Consider visual typography and lateral interpretations, not only lexical substitution.

examples.surface: Two girls seated on someone's knees
examples.lesson: Concrete visual scenes can conceal short name-based charades; check definition precision.

examples.clue: Under tops looking back is a stain (4)
examples.surface: Looking under clothing and discovering a stain
examples.lesson: Let the indicator belong to a misleading scene, not just a mechanical instruction.

examples.clue: Place for pots to be rearranged (4)
examples.lesson: Correct anagrams are not enough; conspicuous indicators and bland surfaces are weak.
